svg.text: Control box inside: Pico 2 and its boards
Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'logic'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: L01: PICO.GP2 -> PICO_CAN.SCK - SPI under 10 cm
L09: PICO.GP22 -> EPS_CAN.CS - GP22 freed from ADS1115 ALERT
L10: PICO.GP26 -> MCP1.SDA - 4.7k pull-ups to 3.3 V, once for the whole bus
L28: MCP2.A1 -> RELAYS2.IN2 - drive lock (opens the KSI line while locked and parked)
L48: PICO.USB -> PI5.USB2_A - Data and reflash only, never power
PI5: Raspberry Pi 5 8GB - The 40-pin header and the PCIe port are kept for the AI HAT+ 2. CAN module wires go to header pins that come up through the HAT
DEBUG: Debug UART header - Inside the box. Vehicle lock workshop reset
PICO_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (control box) - Seeed MCP2515 + SN65HVD230 (3.3 V). Crystal TBC on the bench
EPS_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (steering bus) - Own 500 kbit/s bus to the steering ECU. Transmit only, INT not wired
ADS1: ADS1115 ADC (0x48) - ALERT pin left free so GP22 can be the steering CAN chip select (read "ready" over I2C)
MCP2: Second MCP23017 (0x21) - More outputs for the steering enable and the drive lock relay. The first one is full
ADS2: Second ADS1115 (0x49) - Brake pedal regen only

RELAYS: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8 - One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V
RELAYS2: 16-ch relay board, channels 9-16 (2 used, 6 spare) - Same board as RELAYS. Relay 9 steering enable, relay 10 drive lock (uses the NC contact)
